prompt:
Create a 3x1 sprite sheet for a modern 16-bit-style pixel-art RPG: one MONSTER in three battle poses.

Image 1 is a LAYOUT GUIDE: three cells on white. In each cell the light-grey box shows where the monster stands and how big it is, the grey line is the ground, and the arrow shows the facing: the monster faces RIGHT, toward the heroes. Draw the SAME monster once in every cell, filling its box. Never draw the grey box, line or arrow.

Image 2 is the HOUSE STYLE: an approved hero sprite sheet from this same game. Match its sprite-pixel size, black outlines, flat shading with 2-3 tones per colour and level of detail exactly, but do NOT copy the hero; it is a different character.

Image 3 is an APPROVED MONSTER sheet from this same game (a DIFFERENT monster, idle | attack | hurt): match its sprite-pixel size, rendering, shading, outline weight and level of detail, and how much the poses move. Do NOT copy that monster's body, colours or equipment.

Render as true pixel art: the monster about 96-120 pixels tall in sprite pixels, every sprite pixel a hard-edged square, no anti-aliasing, no gradients.

Monster: a heavy humanoid mechanical soldier of riveted bronze plates, broad shoulders, a barrel-shaped chest, thick jointed legs with flat metal feet, a rounded bronze helm-head with one horizontal glowing amber visor slit, the right arm ending in a long broad metal blade held pointing down at its side, the left arm a three-fingered metal hand; tall and filling the box, centred in its own cell with empty space on both sides, the blade well inside its cell in every cell. Keep every detail identical in every cell. FACE: a rounded bronze helm-head with one glowing amber visor slit.

Cells:
- left cell: idle, a ready battle stance facing right.
- middle cell: attack, stepping forward toward the heroes at the end of a downward chop: the blade arm swung down in front of him with the blade tip on the ground just ahead of his front foot, the body leaning in, the whole blade well inside the middle cell (not raised overhead, not reaching the cell edge), facing right.
- right cell: hurt, knocked back, the body leaning away from the heroes, the blade arm raised up across the chest, the visor flickering, recoiling away from the heroes (leaning left), still facing right.

MOVEMENT: the attack and hurt cells are dramatic ACTION frames, not static stances. Use a strong diagonal line of action through the whole body, shift the weight clearly onto one leg, twist the torso and swing the blade arm with the elbow bent, so every reaching part stays well inside its own cell. Draw only the parts named in the description, the same in every cell: no cape, sparks, steam, smear or motion lines. Each of the three silhouettes must be clearly different. BODY: in every cell, standing on two feet, both feet on the ground line. No mist, smoke or ground effects.

One monster per cell and nothing else: no props on the ground, no effects outside the monster, no text.
Background: solid flat magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, no floor, no shadows, no borders.
Avoid: two creatures in one cell, different creatures in different cells, background scenery, floor tiles, shadows on the ground, magic effects outside the cell, text, frame, border, grid lines, blurry, soft shading, gradient, 3d render, a cannon, a domed head with a lens, teal plates, four legs, a shield, a cape, flesh, a face, sparks, steam.
